title: Chiyya of Hagra
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Yevamot 116a: a bill of divorce was found in Sura in which was written, “In the town of Sura, I, Anan bar Chiyya…” The Rabbis searched from Sura to Nehardea, and there was no other Anan bar Chiyya except Anan bar Chiyya of Hagra. Hyman infers that his son Anan lived in the time of Abaye and Rava. Yuchasin wrote that he lived in Shmuel’s days; possibly its proof is from Ketubot 21a, the document that came out of Mar Shmuel’s court in which was written “when Rav Anan bar Chiyya came,” and Yuchasin perhaps thought that he was the son of Chiyya of Hagra. Hyman distinguishes the two, for the latter was a Torah scholar, while the former was later and there is no proof that he was a Torah scholar.

notes.text: Saved Davidson Yevamot116a contains the Sura/Hagra narrative. Hyman distinguishes the two Anans and argues about their eras and scholarship; no new identity binding follows.

The consulted Yevamot 116a directly names Anan bar Chiyya of Hagra and the Sura–Nehardea investigation. Hyman here distinguishes this Anan from the Shmuel-court witness, whereas his separate Anan notice proposes their identity. Both occurrence-specific arguments remain attributed, without merging the people or silently reconciling the chronology.
